Clinical History:
Knee sprain. [DATE].
Findings:
No significant bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Marginal amputation of the body of the lateral meniscus. Medial meniscus with preserved morphology and signal, no signs of tear.
Cartilage of the femorotibial compartments without alterations.
Thin focal full-thickness chondral ulcer of the inferior aspect of the medial facet of the femoral trochlea with minimal secondary bone changes. Reparative chondral phenomena of the central region of the femoral trochlea. Patellar cartilage without alterations.
Mild joint effusion. No pathological popliteal cysts.
Increased signal at the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon and at the proximal insertion of the patellar tendon, without signs of tear.
No signal abnormalities of Hoffa's fat pad.
Impression:
Marginal amputation of the body of the lateral meniscus.
Grade 4 focal chondropathy of the inferior aspect of the medial facet of the femoral trochlea.
Reparative chondral phenomena of the central region of the femoral trochlea.
Mild joint effusion.
Mild distal quadriceps and proximal patellar tendinosis.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 3.0 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Subchondral insufficiency fracture at the medial margin of the medial tibial plateau without articular surface collapse. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complete radial tear of the posterior root of medial meniscus with mild extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: High-grade cartilage fissuring along the posterior weightbearing medial femoral condyle. Mild marginal spurring at the medial joint line.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Partial inner margin radial tear at the anterior horn/body junction of the lateral meniscus without extrusion.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade cartilage fissuring spanning the weightbearing lateral femoral condyle. High-grade cartilage fissuring along the posterior lateral tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Low-grade cartilage fissuring along the central trochlea. Mild cartilage thinning along the medial patellar facet with mild subchondral cystic change.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild patellar tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 7 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Subchondral insufficiency fracture at the medial margin of the medial tibial plateau without articular surface collapse.
2.	Medial and lateral meniscus tears as described.
3.	Tricompartmental chondrosis.
4.	Small knee effusion.
5.	Mild patellar tendinosis without tear.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion with synovial thickening compatible with synovitis. There is popliteal cyst measuring 21 x 17 x 35 mm. Small amount of edema along the inferior margin of the popliteal cyst suggesting a minimal partial rupture.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
There is increased T2 hyperintense signal within the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending into the posterior horn-body junction without extension to the articular surface, compatible with intrasubstance degeneration. No frank tear.

Mild thickening of the proximal fibers of the medial cruciate ligament, with mild edema, compatible with grade 1 sprain. No frank tear.

Moderate thinning of the articular cartilage of the weightbearing femur and tibia.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
There is a complex degenerative tear of the lateral meniscus with partial maceration of the anterior horn and anterior body, as well as a longitudinal oblique component involving the posterior horn. There is a 4 mm small displaced fragment along the lateral tibial gutter.

Full-thickness fissures in the articular cartilage of the tibial weightbearing surface with associated subchondral bone marrow edema. There is moderate thinning of the articular cartilage of the weightbearing femur and of the tibial plateau. No subchondral bone marrow edema at the femur.

Mild increased signal intensity at the distal iliotibial band. The lateral collateral ligament complex is otherwise unremarkable.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are unremarkable. Mild early intraosseous cystic changes at the tibial insertion of the anterior cruciate ligament.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Multifocal deep and delaminating fissuring of the articular cartilage of the patellar facet without associated subchondral bone marrow edema. Additionally, there is moderate thinning of the articular cartilage of the femoral trochlea without subchondral bone marrow edema.
Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis with mild edema in the suprapatellar fat pad.
Mild patellar tendinosis.

Bones:
Normal.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
Nonspecific edema in the anterior subcutaneous tissues along the infrapatellar region.

Small amount of fluid in the pes anserine bursa.

CONCLUSION:

- Tricompartmental moderate chondral thinning with deep fissures at the lateral and patellofemoral compartments, as described above.
- Complex degenerative tear of the lateral meniscus with tiny displaced fragment.
- Low-grade sprain of the medial collateral ligament.
- Small joint effusion with synovitis.
- Moderate-sized popliteal cyst with minimal partial rupture.

Technique: Knee MRI.
Results: Iliotibial band friction syndrome. Hoffa's fat pad impingement syndrome. Patellar chondropathy.
Impression: Iliotibial band friction syndrome. Hoffa's fat pad impingement syndrome. Patellar chondropathy.

LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of both the medial and lateral meniscus. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Loss of integrity secondary to complete rupture is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Thinning and periligamentous edema are observed in the medial collateral ligament. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. A subarticular nondisplaced fracture and edema in the adjacent bone marrow are observed in the lateral femoral condyle. Contusional bone marrow edema is observed in the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau and in the fibular head. Mild anterior subluxation of the tibia at the tibiofemoral joint is observed. Signal increase due to edema on STIR sequence in the muscle tissue at the proximal portion of the soleus muscle, and increased fluid at the muscle belly is present.
CONCLUSION: Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. Kissing contusion in the tibia and femur and subarticular fracture in the femur. Mild anterior subluxation of the tibia. Grade II meniscopathy in the medial and lateral meniscus. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Suprapatellar bursitis, mild synovitis of the knee joint. Grade I strain of the soleus muscle.

Right knee pain. R/O ACL insufficiency. 
MRI of right knee without contrast. 
Pulse sequences: sagittal T1, axial, coronal, sagittal T2 FS, sagittal PD FS

Findings: 
1. Suggestive of complete tear of ACL. 
The PCL appears intact. 
2. Tear of the posterior horn of medial meniscus.
The lateral meniscus shows no obvious tear. Suspected meniscocapsular separation over posterior horn of lateral meniscus. 
3. The medial & lateral collateral ligaments, quadriceps & patellar tendons show intact appearance. 
4. Mild to moderate knee joint effusion. 
5. Bone marrow edema over lateral tibial plateau. 
Periarticular & intraarticular soft tissue edema mainly over prepatellar & infrapatellar area. 
6. Intact patellar cartilage. 

IMP:
Complete ACL tear. 
Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus. 
Suspected meniscocapsular separation over posterior horn of lateral meniscus. 
Mild to moderate knee joint effusion. 
Bone marrow edema over lateral tibial plateau.

Suggest clinical correlation and further management.

text:
Advanced gonarthrotic changes with extensive joint effusion and moderate synovial proliferation.
Bone marrow reconversion zones in the femoral metaphysis.
Cartilage denudation of the medial compartment of the femorotibial joint and fissures and erosions of the cartilage of the lateral compartment.
Chondromalacia grade III of both patellar facets and the femoral trochlea, with reduced thickness of the aforementioned cartilages and extensive osteophytes of the patellofemoral joint – described as part of the aforementioned OA changes.
The visualized articular bodies are appropriately articulated.
Complex tear of both menisci with bilateral extrusion of approximately 5 mm, both menisci significantly degenerative.
Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
The posterior cruciate ligament is markedly edematous in its proximal 2/3, thickened (width 12 mm), with multiple ganglion cysts up to 7 mm in diameter at the tibial insertion. – Differential diagnosis: due to advanced degenerative changes or an older partial tear.
The lateral collateral ligament is fusiformly thickened at its insertion on the lateral femoral epicondyle and shows altered signal intensity at its insertion on the fibular head, possibly representing a prior partial tear or enthesopathic changes.
The medial collateral ligament is fusiformly thickened at its insertion on the medial femoral epicondyle with periligamentous edema, likely due to enthesopathic changes.
The popliteus tendon is edematous with altered signal intensity, consistent with tendinopathy.
Normal appearance of the iliotibial tract and pes anserinus.
The quadriceps tendon and patellar ligament show altered signal intensity at their insertions on the patella, with maintained continuity – enthesopathic changes.
The patellar retinacula are intact.
Popliteal cyst measuring 5 mm in diameter.

text: Signs of disuse osteopenia as well as residual bone bruise in the posterolateral tibial plateau near the eminence with subchondral impression and partly focal chondral lesions. Historically known ACL rupture with likely ligamentous rupture of the anteromedial bundle and bony avulsion of the posterolateral bundle (4/23). Additional ossicle/flake adjacent to the not clearly delineable lateral meniscus posterior horn root, here DD also involvement/bony avulsion. Medial meniscus with horizontal tear extending from the pars intermedia into the posterior horn with mucoid degeneration. Additionally bone edema in the medial femorotibial compartment, marginal, predominantly tibial, with primarily chondropathy. Accompanying mild joint effusion, reactive synovitis, and mildly fluid-filled Baker's cyst with CC 3.2 cm. Small mediopatellar plica.
